method: All28group two-frame profiles visually inspected across7complete overview pages; E01/E10/E11/E15 also inspected as full detailed figures. Plot labels were subsequently separated to remove overlap; numerical data unchanged.

E01.reason: Repeated neighboring peak pattern aligns better in approximate topocentric coordinates. Terrestrial/instrumental hypothesis remains open; frame preference alone does not identify a physical mechanism. Only a10-day baseline is available here, so this is weaker frame discrimination than E10/E11.

E02.reason: Broad peak and neighboring troughs recur in all selected epochs, including exposures not carrying an original unresolved hit. This supports a persistent spectral-structure interpretation; it does not by itself identify emission versus absorption windows or a natural line species. Both frames correlate strongly over this limited barycentric-velocity span, so frame discrimination is weaker than profile persistence.
